settings.event_id: md5 of content after masking BlockId, IP, and digits
settings.settings_source: Reused the HDFS_2k validation-selected Isolation Forest settings. An 8-config grid on hundreds of thousands of train blocks was not rerun.
labels_used_for: excluding known anomalies from IF training when train_on=normal

baseline_held_out_blocks.pr_auc_note: Average precision on Isolation Forest scores (threshold-independent).

improved_validation_blocks.pr_auc_note: Average precision on Isolation Forest scores (threshold-independent).

improved_held_out_blocks.pr_auc_note: Average precision on Isolation Forest scores (threshold-independent).

comparison.note: Improved uses the 2k-selected Isolation Forest settings plus a validation threshold. Baseline uses contamination=0.05 on the original feature set, fit on train blocks only. Deltas are measured, not assumed.

limitations: HDFS_v1 parquet rows have no official Drain EventId; EventId is a masked-content hash.
Lines that mention several blocks keep only the first BlockId, matching the 2k demo.
Block label is the max of the parquet `anomaly` flag (1 if any line in the block is labelled anomalous).
The 8-config Isolation Forest grid from HDFS_2k was not rerun on the full corpus.
Validation thresholds on large splits use score quantiles, not every unique score.
EventId one-hot width is capped at 64 values fit on train blocks only.
Isolation Forest is unsupervised; labels are not used as a supervised training target.
The live dashboard, /api/stats, /api/anomalies, and /api/retrain still serve HDFS_2k only.
A small held-out F1 delta is not a claim of improvement. Compare PR-AUC as well; the two can disagree.
Masked-content hashing can collapse official Drain templates into fewer EventIds.
